title: The analytical sample
alt: Counts of firearm robbery, assault and battery events in the main Chicago sample
description: The main sample contains 94,207 mutually exclusive firearm robbery, assault and battery records.

title: Monthly trends differ by offence
alt: Monthly Chicago event counts for firearm robbery, assault and battery from 2015 to 2024
description: Robbery, assault and battery follow distinct long-term patterns, supporting category-specific analysis.

title: The week, hour by hour
alt: Heatmap of Chicago firearm-involved events by hour and weekday
description: Activity is lowest during weekday mornings and rises through afternoons and evenings, with visible late-night weekend concentration.

title: Seasonal signatures by category
alt: Annual and seasonal patterns for robbery, assault and battery in Chicago
description: The offence categories differ in both their development over time and their seasonal peaks.

title: Where events concentrate
alt: Community-area maps of firearm robbery, assault and battery in Chicago
description: Persistent geographic concentration differs by offence category across Chicago’s 77 community areas.

title: Highest-count community areas
alt: Top ten Chicago community areas for firearm robbery, assault and battery
description: A limited group of community areas accounts for a substantial share of recorded events.

title: Recent exposure across area boundaries
alt: Estimated rate ratios for adjacent, non-adjacent and same-area exposure across time lags
description: Same-area and cross-area histories are predictive, but adjacent exposure is not consistently stronger than non-adjacent exposure.

title: A modest predictive gain
alt: Percentage improvement in test Poisson deviance across spillover model specifications
description: Adding the complete cross-area history produces a maximum out-of-sample deviance reduction of about 1.3%.

title: Geography beats random neighbours
alt: Observed geographic adjacency compared with random-neighbour placebo networks
description: Chicago’s observed adjacency network carries more short-term information than randomized neighbour networks.

title: Exposure weakens with distance
alt: Change in gun-violence exposure lift across community-area distance bands
description: The descriptive exposure lift is strongest among nearby areas, adding nuance to the boundary-based result.

title: Philadelphia replication
description: This slot is reserved for the thesis figure comparing confirmed-shooting distance profiles in Chicago and Philadelphia.
